item.title: Bengali filmmaker Anik Dutta dies at 66 after falling from terrace
item.description:
Acclaimed Bengali filmmaker Anik Dutta died on Wednesday afternoon at a private hospital in South Kolkata after suffering critical injuries in a fall from the terrace of his wife’s residence near Gariahat, family members confirmed. He was 66.
Dutta was taken to a nearby hospital in a critical condition following the incident but later succumbed to multiple injuries.
The filmmaker, grandson of Narendra Chandra Dutta, made his directorial debut with the acclaimed political satire Bhooter Bhabishyat in 2012. The film earned widespread praise for its unique blend of humor, political commentary, and social satire, establishing him as a prominent filmmaker in the Bengali film industry.
Over the years, Dutta directed several notable films, including "Aschorjo Prodip", "Borunbabur Bondhu", and "Aparajito."
Released on the 101st birth anniversary of legendary filmmaker Satyajit Ray, Aparajito paid tribute to Ray’s life and cinematic legacy. A devoted admirer of Ray, Dutta often reflected the celebrated filmmaker’s influence in his own storytelling and cinematic style.
Known for his left-leaning political views, Dutta was also an outspoken critic of the government led by Mamata Banerjee.
His differences with the West Bengal government intensified in 2019 following the release controversy surrounding Bhobishyoter Bhoot, regarded as a spiritual successor to his debut film. The movie was allegedly prevented from screening in theaters, prompting protests and legal action.
Later, India’s Supreme Court directed the West Bengal government to pay Rs 20 lakh in compensation to the film’s producer, Kalyanmoy Billy Chatterjee, and imposed an additional fine of Rs 1 lakh on the state. In its observation, the court said, “Free speech cannot be gagged for fear of the mob.”
Dutta’s final directorial work was Joto Kando Kolkatatei, featuring actors Abir Chatterjee, Quazi Nawshaba Ahmed, and Dulal Lahiri in key roles.

item.title: Home minister’s intervention saves ‘Donald Trump’ from Eid sacrifice
item.description:
The viral albino buffalo named “Donald Trump” will ultimately not be sacrificed during Eid-ul-Azha, following the intervention of Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed.
The buffalo is being returned from the buyer and taken back to its farm in Narayanganj.
The information was confirmed on Wednesday by Faisal Hasan, deputy chief information officer of the Ministry of Home Affairs.
He said the decision was made due to concerns over excessive public gatherings and possible disorder surrounding the buffalo. The buyer from Keraniganj has been refunded, and for now, “Donald Trump” will continue to be raised at the farm as before.
The nearly 700-kilogram albino buffalo, raised at Rabeya Agro Farm in Paikpara, Narayanganj, gained widespread attention on social media. Its white fur and hairstyle reminded many people of US President Donald Trump , leading to the nickname “Donald Trump.”
Earlier on Monday afternoon, the buffalo was handed over to its buyer in a grand ceremony arranged by the farm. The animal received a “royal farewell” featuring a red carpet, colorful smoke effects, and special decorations. Later, the buyer, Samir from the Jinjira area of Dhaka, took it to the capital.
According to the farm authorities, the buffalo was sold at Tk550 per kilogram as live weight. The four-year-old buffalo weighed around 690 kilograms.
After going viral, crowds from distant areas flocked to the farm to see the buffalo. In addition to Bangladeshi media outlets, international news organizations including Reuters , Agence France-Presse , New York Post , France 24 , and Gulf News also published reports on it.

item.title: Ad-Din Hospital: 6 child deaths were accidental
item.description:
Six children died at the Ad-Din Medical College Hospital in the capital's Moghbazar, which the hospital authorities have claimed as accidental.
On Wednesday morning, DMP Ramna Division Assistant Police Commissioner Mazharul Islam said that there were a total of 11 mothers and 6 children in the hospital's post-operative room.
Around 2:00-3:00 am, a mother asked to turn off the AC because she felt too cold. Later, the AC was turned off for an hour. At that time, other children developed breathing problems.
Later, around 6 am, the children's condition started to deteriorate and six children died one by one, he stated.
Islam told the media that an investigation team including the police crime team is at the scene. How the children died is being investigated.
According to police sources, the children who died are one to two days old. All were in the post-operative ward.
After the incident, the hospital's Director General (Hospitals and Nursing) Professor Dr. Nahida Yeasmin held a press conference in the afternoon. She said that the ward where this accidental death occurred had 11 mothers and six newborn babies. The children were probably one to two days old.
She also said that mothers and babies are always kept in that ward after a cesarean section.
In addition, one more person can stay with them. Since it is an AC ward, it is often cold. Patients and their relatives often ask the nurse to turn off the AC if they feel excessively cold.
Professor Dr Yeasmin said that when two children suddenly felt sick, they were taken to the hospital's Neonatal ICU.
Seeing them after 3:00AM, the doctors said that the children were fine. After that, they were asked to take them to the ward.
She also said that after 6:00 am, the nurses and mothers in charge saw that the children's condition was worsening.
After that, all six children were taken to the Neonatal ICU. After being taken there, two children were found dead. The remaining four children were kept on ventilator support in a sick state. Despite doctors' efforts, those four children could not be saved, she added.

item.title: Nimni becomes third Bangladeshi woman to summit Everest
item.description:
Bangladeshi mountaineer Nurunnaher Nimni has become the third Bangladeshi woman to successfully summit Mount Everest, the world’s highest peak.
According to the Bangladesh Mountaineering and Trekking Club (BMITC), she reached the 29,032-foot summit at 5:24am Nepal time on Wednesday, raising the national flag at the world’s highest peak.
Nimni began her journey from Dhaka on April 11 and reached the Everest base camp after a challenging expedition. She initially reached Camp IV on 23 May but had to descend due to adverse weather conditions.
She resumed her final ascent on May 25 when conditions improved and completed the climb early Wednesday morning.
Nepal on Wednesday congratulated Bangladeshi mountaineer Nurunnahar Nimni on successfully scaling Mount Everest.
"Hearty congratulations to Bangladeshi mountaineer Nurunnahar Nimni on successfully scaling Mount Everest this morning," said the Embassy of Nepal.
"We wish her continued success in all her future endeavors," it said.
On 19 May 2012, Nishat Majumdar became the first Bangladeshi woman to summit Mount Everest, with Wasfia Nazreen following just days later on 26 May the same year.
After a 14-year gap for Bangladeshi women climbers on Everest, Nurunnaher Nimni has now reached the summit, becoming the only Bangladeshi climber to achieve the feat so far in 2026.

item.title: Minister: Eid travel smooth despite massive holiday rush
item.description:
Road Transport and Bridges Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam said millions of people have left the capital ahead of Eid-ul-Azha, while the overall holiday travel situation remains under satisfactory management despite heavy pressure on roads, railways and waterways.
He also said the transportation of nearly 8 million sacrificial animals is continuing smoothly.
The minister made the comments to journalists on Wednesday after visiting the Mohakhali Bus Terminal in Dhaka. He said nearly 15 million people are leaving Dhaka within two to three days, creating a major management challenge. Despite this, the government is working in coordination across road, rail and water transport systems to reduce public suffering.
He said the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority’s (BRTA) central control room is monitoring the transport situation round the clock. Authorities are taking immediate action if complaints of overcharging or irregularities are received. He also claimed that most passengers are travelling at government-fixed fares.
Regarding traffic congestion in the Chandra area before the Jamuna Bridge, the minister said traffic is slowing because vehicles from seven lanes are merging into two lanes. However, he described it as a normal situation during the Eid rush rather than a major problem.
He also said 51 additional coaches have been added to trains to ensure smoother Eid travel. Separate coaches for women have also been introduced on several intercity trains operating on the Dhaka-Chattogram, Dhaka-Sylhet and Dhaka-Mymensingh routes.

item.title: Daughter seeks parole release for Dipu Moni as father falls critically ill
item.description:
Former education minister Dipu Moni ’s daughter has applied for her seven-day parole release on humanitarian grounds, citing the critical illness of her father.
The application was submitted on Wednesday to the Munshiganj deputy commissioner by Tani Dipaboli Nawaz, daughter of Dipu Moni.
Confirming the matter, Dipu Moni’s lawyer Gazi Faisal Islam said she is currently detained at Munshiganj District Jail, while her husband is in critical condition.
“Her daughter has sought a seven-day parole release so she can be by his side,” he said.
According to the application, Dipu Moni was arrested on August 20, 2024, in a case filed with Mohammadpur Police Station. She was later shown arrested in 37 more cases and has remained imprisoned in Munshiganj District Jail since then as an accused in multiple under-investigation cases.
The application states that her husband, Towfiq Nawaz, is suffering from severe health complications, including cancer, liver disease and stroke-related conditions. He is currently undergoing treatment in the CCU of a private hospital in the capital in critical condition. His health reportedly deteriorated sharply after a blood transfusion on Tuesday.
The petition further says Dipu Moni has been in jail for nearly 21 months and has been unable to remain beside her husband during his prolonged illness. It argues that her presence is urgently needed to oversee his treatment and support him during this critical period.
The application also states that, on humanitarian grounds, she should be granted seven days’ parole to care for her seriously ill husband and remain beside him if his condition worsens further.
Following the fall of the Awami League government, police arrested Dipu Moni on August 19, 2024. She has remained in custody since then.

item.title: Dhaka-TangailJamuna bridge highway returns to normal after 20 hours of gridlock
item.description:
After nearly 20 hours of severe traffic congestion, the Dhaka–Tangail–Jamuna Bridge highway returned to normal on Wednesday night.
Traffic movement became smooth around 9pm, and vehicles are now moving without major disruption.
Earlier, on the final day of the Eid journey, the highway experienced intense congestion due to excessive traffic pressure, breakdowns of several vehicles on the Jamuna Bridge, road accidents and rain, causing immense suffering for homebound passengers.
Police worked tirelessly to ease the situation.
Police and Jamuna Bridge authorities said severe congestion had started in the Chandra area of Gazipur on Wednesday night, which later affected the Tangail stretch. Long queues of vehicles formed from the Jamuna Bridge to Mirzapur, creating nearly 50km of traffic jam.
Although congestion in Chandra later eased, the Tangail section remained heavily affected. As the day progressed, traffic pressure increased further and several minor accidents occurred, eventually bringing movement on the highway to a near standstill.
To improve northbound travel, authorities repeatedly implemented one-way traffic through the Jamuna Bridge from morning, which gradually reduced congestion in the afternoon. By 9pm, traffic flow fully normalized.
In the last 24 hours, 56,239 vehicles crossed the bridge, generating toll revenue of Tk38,29,97,050.
Passengers said it took 16 to 18 hours to cross the Jamuna Bridge section, causing severe suffering for women, children, the elderly and the sick. They urged a permanent solution to such recurring Eid travel congestion.
Elenga Police Outpost In-Charge Md Sharif said the highway became normal after 8pm, with no traffic jam or slow movement at present. Police and highway authorities worked continuously to manage the situation.

item.title: How will the weather be on Eid day?
item.description:
Adverse weather may disrupt the joy of Eid-ul-Azha, as the Bangladesh Meteorological Department has forecast light to moderate rain across much of Bangladesh, including Dhaka, on Thursday morning.
The BMD said that many areas in the Rangpur, Rajshahi, Dhaka, Mymensingh, Khulna and Sylhet divisions may experience temporary gusty or squally winds accompanied by light to moderate rain or thundershowers. In some places, moderate to heavy rainfall is also likely.
Rain or thundershowers may also occur in parts of the Barisal and Chittagong divisions. The department added that daytime temperatures may slightly drop due to rainfall, while nighttime temperatures could rise marginally.
Meteorologist Tariful Newaz said Dhaka may see light to moderate rain on Eid morning, with relatively calm weather in the afternoon before rain returns again in the evening or at night.
Meanwhile, a low-pressure area is likely to form over the east-central Bay of Bengal, which may continue to bring rainfall for two to three days after Eid, according to the weather office.

item.title: Four killed in separate road accidents in Bogra
item.description:
Four people, including a bus supervisor, two truck helpers, and a factory worker, were killed and several others injured in separate road accidents in Bogra’s Kahaloo and Nondigram upazilas from Tuesday night to Wednesday morning.
The information was confirmed by Hafizar Rahman, officer-in-charge of Kunderhat Highway Police Station, and Mahbubur Rahman, investigation officer of Kahaloo Police Station.
The deceased were identified as Uttam Mondal, 30, supervisor of Hanif Paribahan and son of Jitendra Nath Mondal of Komarpur village in Badalgachhi upazila of Naogaon; Md Hridoy, 30, a truck helper and son of Abdur Razzak of Malshun village in Adamdighi upazila of Bogra; Md Injamam, 20, another truck helper and son of Izzat Ali of Kharashni village in the Sadar upazila of Jhenaidah; and factory worker Robiul Awal Zia, 42, son of Abdur Razzak of Torotbari village in Birganj upazila of Dinajpur.
Police and locals said a Naogaon-bound Hanif Paribahan bus from Dhaka suffered a tire puncture in the Boubazar area under Narhatta union of Kahaloo upazila on Tuesday night. The bus was standing beside the Bogra-Naogaon highway when a truck coming from behind lost control and rammed into it. Both vehicles fell into a roadside ditch, leaving several people injured, including bus supervisor Uttam Mondal and truck helper Md Hridoy.
Fire service personnel rescued the injured and took them to Bogra Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College Hospital. Uttam Mondal died while undergoing treatment around 4:15am on Wednesday, while Md Hridoy died around 8:15am.
Earlier on Wednesday morning, a sand-laden truck traveling from Bogra to Natore crashed into another stationary sand-filled truck at the Fakpal intersection in Nondigram upazila after the driver lost control around 6:15am. The front part of the truck was badly mangled, trapping driver Shamim Sheikh and helper Md Injamam inside.
Members of Nondigram Fire Service and Civil Defence rescued them and took them to Bogra Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared truck helper Injamam dead.
Meanwhile, around midnight on Tuesday, factory worker Robiul Awal Zia was killed after being hit by an unidentified vehicle while attempting to cross the Bogra-Naogaon highway in the Bhyapra area under Narhatta union of Kahaloo upazila. He worked at the New Hope Feed Mill factory in the area.
Kahaloo Police Station Investigation Officer Mahbubur Rahman said the unidentified vehicle fled immediately after the accident. Efforts are underway to identify the vehicle and arrest its driver.
He added that the accident-hit bus and trucks have been seized, and separate cases have been filed under the Road Transport Act.

item.title: State minister denies space for cattle market leased out under Diabari metro rail station
item.description:
State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam on Tuesday said no space beneath or around the metro rail station in the capital's Diabari area had been leased out for cattle trading.
The state minister made the comments while visiting the Diabari cattle market in Uttara in Wednesday afternoon.
“We have not leased out any space under or around this metro rail station for a cattle market,” he said.
According to him, some traders temporarily took shelter under the metro rail station with their cattle following heavy rainfall two days ago.
“Later, the administrator of Dhaka North City Corporation personally came and removed the cattle from the road to the designated market area,” he added.
The minister said magistrates were working on-site round the clock and alleged that a video recorded three days earlier had been circulated on social media in an attempt to create controversy surrounding the government.
“You can visit the spot and see for yourselves that cattle trading is taking place only inside the designated market,” he said.
He acknowledged that some parts of the road became dirty after cattle moved onto the streets but said cleaning operations had begun since morning.
“City corporation staff and law enforcement personnel are working here continuously. No cattle trading will be allowed around the metro rail area. We have already removed the cattle, and such activities will not be allowed in the future," he said.
The state minister also said the government had repeatedly instructed that cattle markets must remain within designated boundaries.
“Whenever such issues have come to our notice, we have taken immediate action. Public cooperation is also needed,” he added.
During the visit, Md Shafiqul Islam Khan, administrator of Dhaka North City Corporation, said some traders had gathered under the metro rail station during rainfall but were removed immediately.
“Later, after learning that cattle traders had returned to the spot, I visited the area again at around 1:30am and took action.
Cleaning activities have been ongoing since this morning,” he said.

item.title: Women rights activists call for accountability over Bangladesh Betar dress code directive
item.description:
A group of women rights activists, academics, artists and civil society members have expressed concern over a recently issued Bangladesh Betar directive on dress code for news presenters, even though the instruction has since been withdrawn.
In an open letter addressed to Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapan, they welcomed the decision to cancel the directive issued on May 4, 2026, which had set specific clothing guidelines for female news presenters, including wearing saree or salwar-kameez with dupatta, while discouraging “large bindis” and wearing the dupatta on one side.
The signatories, however, said merely withdrawing the directive was not enough, arguing that the mindset behind such instructions also needs to be critically reviewed. They described the directive as culturally insensitive and contrary to women’s dignity, rights and constitutional values of equality, personal freedom and cultural inclusion.
They also said such restrictions reinforce harmful social norms, discriminatory attitudes and controlling behaviour towards women in workplaces.
The letter further called for accountability for those involved in drafting and issuing the directive and urged authorities to ensure inclusive, respectful and discrimination-free workplace policies in the future.
Although the directive has been withdrawn, the signatories said it should be kept in mind for future consideration and proposed the following recommendations:
The open letter was signed by 53 individuals, including Khushi Kabir; human rights activist, Farah Kabir; country director, ActionAid Bangladesh, Shaheen Anam; human rights activist and executive director, Manusher Jonno Foundation, Mahin Sultan; Nari Pokkho, Rani Yen Yen; indigenous rights activist.

item.title: Bangladesh ready for SAFF Women’s Championship opener on Eid day
item.description:
Defending champions Bangladesh are ready to begin their campaign in the SAFF Women’s Championship 2026 when they take on Maldives in their opening Group B match in Goa, India on Thursday.
The match carries added significance as it coincides with Eid-ul-Azha in Bangladesh, with the nation’s women footballers hoping to celebrate the occasion by making a winning start in their bid for a third consecutive South Asian title.
Bangladesh lifted their maiden SAFF Women’s Championship crown in 2022 before retaining the trophy in 2024, defeating hosts Nepal in the final on both occasions.
Now blending experienced campaigners with emerging young talents, the Tigresses enter the tournament with confidence, although they are expected to face stiff competition from five-time champions India, who opened their campaign with a commanding 11-0 victory over Maldives.
Bangladesh head coach Peter Butler, however, brushed aside any discussion of chasing a similar scoreline against the Maldives.
“It’s marathon, it’s not sprint,” Butler said on Wednesday while speaking about the team’s approach to the tournament.
“It’s first match. We just take one game at a time,” added the English coach, whose side will also face hosts India in their second and final group-stage fixture on May 31.
Earlier during the pre-tournament press conference, Butler expressed satisfaction with Bangladesh’s preparation and said he hoped the work done ahead of the tournament would help the defending champions retain the title once again.
The tournament also marks the beginning of a new chapter for midfielder Maria Manda, who has taken over the captaincy from Afeida Khandaker.
“We all are fit,” Maria said on Wednesday.
“As it is our first match, our target is to take the points. We all are ready to try and play well,” she added.
Asked whether the team wanted to give the fans back home an Eid gift through their performance, Maria responded positively.
“Of course, if we do well, it is like giving something to the country. We expect to play well and gift a good performance as well as a good result,” said the Bangladesh skipper.
The match will be played at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium and is scheduled to kick off at 8pm Bangladesh Standard Time.
Six nations are competing in this year’s tournament, divided into two groups. Bangladesh, India and Maldives are placed in Group B, while Nepal, Bhutan and Sri Lanka make up Group A.
The semi-finals are scheduled for June 3, with the final set to be held on June 6.

item.title: 'Watchword is team’: De la Fuente warns talent alone won’t win World Cup for Spain
item.description:
Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente believes reigning European champions Spain still have significant room for growth ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, insisting that technical brilliance alone will not be enough to conquer football’s biggest stage.
Speaking to FIFA less than a month before Spain begin their campaign against Cabo Verde in Atlanta, De la Fuente stressed the importance of teamwork, maturity and balance within his youthful squad.
“There’s still plenty of room for improvement. We have a hugely gifted group of players, but many of them are very young. Blending them with the more experienced figures in the squad has provided stability and a clear sense of direction,” said De la Fuente.
Spain enter the tournament as one of the favourites after winning the European Championship and boasting a talented generation led by teenage sensation Lamine Yamal.
However, De la Fuente warned that individual quality alone does not guarantee tournament success.
“For me, the watchword is ‘team’. That must take precedence over individual talent, which should always serve the team,” he said.
“Individual talent alone is not enough to win big competitions. You can win matches, but not tournaments.”
The 64-year old coach, who has worked with many current Spain players since their youth-team days, said the close bond within the squad is one of their greatest strengths.
“I’ve witnessed every stage of their development and we’ve grown together. It transcends the normal relationship between a player and coach,” he explained.
The former youth coach also highlighted the importance of maintaining composure under pressure at the World Cup.
“You can do almost everything right and still lose at this level. The players need to stay calm, take responsibility, be professional and show team spirit,” he added.
De la Fuente reserved special praise for Yamal, who made his Spain debut at just 16 and is expected to be one of the stars of the tournament.
“He’s hungry to grow and improve and he sets high standards, especially for himself,” said the Spain boss.
Asked what success would look like at the World Cup, De la Fuente emphasised commitment over promises of silverware.
“Playing every match as if it’s our last, respecting our opponents and being ready to challenge for the highest honours,” he said.
“The only things we ask for are effort, hard work and dedication. The results will take care of themselves.”

item.title: 'Swaying in the wind': Giant Messi statue in India to be removed over safety concerns
item.description:
A giant statue of football superstar Lionel Messi erected in India to mark his visit last year is "swaying in the wind" and will be removed, a lawmaker told AFP on Wednesday.
Workers have scrambled up the 21-metre (70-foot) golden-coloured statue in the eastern city of Kolkata in West Bengal, throwing ropes around its shoulders to secure it.
The sculpture showing the 38-year-old Argentina and Inter Miami star raising the World Cup trophy was unveiled during Messi's so-called GOAT Tour of India in December.
But West Bengal state legislator Sharadwat Mukherjee said it was no longer safe.
"The statue of the Argentine football legend in the city of Kolkata was found unsafe by engineers of the West Bengal government," he said.
"We have noticed that the statue is swaying in the wind."
Workers on Wednesday used ropes to attempt to secure the statue, which looms over a busy road.
Mukherjee said it was not clear when it would be brought down.
"Removal has proved easier said than done," he said. "We are planning to remove the statue at the earliest opportunity."
He did not say whether the statue would be re-erected at another site.

item.title: Argentina coach Scaloni encouraged by news on Messi injury
item.description:
Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the initial news regarding superstar Lionel Messi's fitness "is not that bad" and hopes further examinations will confirm that diagnosis with the World Cup just a fortnight away.
Messi has been diagnosed with muscle fatigue in his left hamstring by his Major League Soccer club Inter Miami after he made an abrupt exit from Miami's 6-4 victory over Philadelphia in the 73rd minute on Sunday.
Even at 38 and eying a sixth World Cup finals appearance, Messi remains the side's talisman for the defence of the title they won in Qatar four years ago.
"Obviously we would have preferred that nothing had happened," Scaloni told Argentinian TV station DSports on Tuesday.
"Now one has to wait and see how it evolves and above all the new tests they are going to conduct in order to see if it confirms their original diagnosis."
Scaloni, who is due to name his squad next week, added he had watched the match on TV at the federation's headquarters and been relieved that Messi had asked to come off.
Inter manager Guillermo Hoyos explained after the match Messi was tired, the pitch was heavy and no-one wanted to take a risk with his fitness.
Inter Miami issued a statement on Monday saying: "The timeline for his return to physical activity will depend on his clinical and functional progress."
That gave little indication about the status of the eight-time Ballon D'Or winner.
Argentina are set to begin their World Cup campaign on June 16 against Algeria in Kansas City.
They then play Austria on June 22 and round off their Group J campaign against Jordan on June 28.
Messi has managed his workload since joining Inter Miami in 2023, with team staff regularly excusing him from matches in congested fixture periods.
MLS has started a break in its season for the World Cup, which is co-hosted by the United States, Mexico and Canada.
Messi has not formally confirmed he plans to play in the World Cup, but is widely expected to return for what would be a record-matching sixth appearance at the finals.
His great Portuguese rival Cristiano Ronaldo and potentially Mexican goalkeeper Guillermo Ochoa would also be making a sixth appearance.
Argentina are set to play two pre-World Cup friendlies against Honduras on June 6 and Iceland on June 9, both in the United States.

item.title: Bangladesh batters win big on latest update to Test rankings
item.description:
Bangladesh's recent ICC World Test Championship series triumph over Pakistan has helped a host of their red-ball stars make big gains on the latest ICC Men's Test Player Rankings.
The Asian side registered an emphatic 2-0 series win over their close rival and moved up to fifth place on the World Test Championship standings as a result.
Veteran right-hander Mushfiqur Rahim led the way for Bangladesh with a series-best 259 runs from four innings and that helped the evergreen 39-year-old move up 10 spots to equal 16th on the latest list for Test batters.
Mushfiqur wasn't the only Bangladesh batter to make gains, with fellow right-hander Litton Das moving up 14 spots to 24th following his haul of 239 runs across the series.
It was a similar story on the updated rankings for Test bowlers, with Bangladesh trio Taijul Islam (up two places to 11th with a new career-high rating, Mehidy Hasan (up two slots to 25th) and Nahid Rana (up 10 spots to 54th all rising the updated charts following some impressive hauls against Pakistan.
Taijul also gained three spots to move to 29th on the list for Test all-rounders, while Pakistan will be buoyed by the fact that Khurram Shahzad re-entered the Test bowler rankings in 49th place after he made his first Test appearance since the start of 2025 during the second fixture in Sylhet.
There were also some changes to the updated ODI rankings following the completion of a tri-series that featured Nepal, USA and Scotland as part of the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 competition.
Hosts Nepal picked up three victories during the tri-series and Aasif Sheikh (up five spots to equal 81st) and Dipendra Singh Airee (up eight places to equal 91st) were rewarded as they made ground on the latest rankings for ODI batters as a result.
Nepal teammates Sandeep Lamichhane (up four slots to 32nd) and Lalit Rajbanshi (up six spots to equal 47th) made eye-catching improvement on the list for ODI bowlers, while Scotland were boosted by gains for star all-rounder Brandon McMullen (up four rungs to 49th) on the list for ODI batters.
USA spinner Nosthush Kenjige (up 10 slots to 49th) was among those who made ground on the list for ODI bowlers, while teammate Milind Kumar (up four places to equal 18th) was the big mover on the list for ODI all-rounders.

item.title: Tanners anxious over waste treatment, rising costs ahead of Eid-ul-Azha
item.description:
Despite entering their peak business season ahead of Eid-ul-Azha, tannery owners at the Savar Leather Industrial Estate are gripped by anxiety over inadequate waste treatment facilities and a sharp increase in the prices of salt and processing chemicals.
Industry stakeholders report that ongoing challenges in achieving international environmental certification and heavy reliance on a single export market are casting a shadow over the sector's prospects.
According to data from the Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock, more than 12.3 million animals are available for sacrifice nationwide this year, including approximately 5.7 million cattle and buffaloes, and over 6.6 million goats and sheep.
The total number of sacrifices is projected to exceed 10 million, with the vast majority of the resulting hides expected to be processed at the BSCIC Leather Industrial Estate in Harindhara, Savar.
During a visit to the estate on Tuesday (May 26), authorities were observed renovating the Central Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP), clearing drainage networks, and digging two temporary ponds to manage the imminent surge in solid and liquid waste.
While individual factories have stockpiled essential chemicals such as sodium sulfide, hydrated lime, and basic chromium sulfate, tannery owners expressed deep concern over the soaring cost of salt, the primary preservative for rawhides.
Industry sources state that the sector requires 80,000 to 85,000 tonnes of salt for the season.
Although the government has distributed approximately 11,500 tonnes of free salt to charities and orphanages, market prices for a 74-kilogram bag of salt have surged by Tk250, currently retailing between Tk930 and Tk950.
"The government has fixed the procurement price of raw hides between Tk60 and Tk70 per square foot, but selling at that rate in the current market is highly unrealistic," said Ripon Chowdhury, a local tannery owner.
"International market rates are hovering around $0.40 per square foot, and we cannot sell finished leather for more than Tk35 to Tk40. Given the high production costs, buying raw hides at the government-mandated price is commercially unviable."
A major structural issue highlighted by tanners is Bangladesh’s heavy dependence on the Chinese market, which limits local bargaining power.
"We are entirely reliant on China, and we have to accept whatever price they dictate," said Zakir Hossain, an official at Angela Tannery.
"Until we can secure Leather Working Group (LWG) certification and enter the European market, it will be incredibly difficult for this industry to turn a profit. The modern compliance measures promised during our relocation from Hazaribagh have still not been fully implemented."
Operational uncertainties also extend to infrastructure.
"We have prepared our salt and chemical reserves, but continuous electricity remains a major concern," said Ayub, an official at Ayub Brothers Tannery. "Without an uninterrupted power supply, a significant portion of the collected hides will rot."
Meanwhile, factory workers claim that the relocation to Savar has failed to improve working and living conditions.
"We relocated here in 2017, yet there is still no medical center, proper pharmacy, school, or recreational space for workers within this 200-acre industrial zone," said Mohammad Manik, a tannery worker.
Bangladesh Tanners Association (BTA) senior vice-president Shakawat Ullah stated that the national collection target for this season has been set at 10 million hides.
He urged grassroots traders and seasonal buyers to apply salt immediately after slaughter to preserve the quality of the leather before transporting it to the tanneries.
